nodes.label: Eco-label awareness

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Eco-label awareness_qna_000
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: Why do consumers with relatively poor knowledge of eco label production standards still have positive attitudes towards eco labelled products?
nodes.answer: Consumers with relatively poor knowledge of eco label production standards still have positive attitudes towards eco labelled products because they believe that these products are healthier and more environmentally friendly.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Eco-label awareness_qna_001
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How does education level influence consumer behaviour towards eco labelled products?
nodes.answer: Consumers with higher education have a better understanding of sustainability labels, are more sensitive to environmental issues, and are frequently more willing to buy labelled products.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Eco-label awareness_qna_002
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why is low sustainability and label knowledge a barrier for labels?
nodes.answer: Low sustainability and label knowledge hinder consumer understanding and attention.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Eco-label awareness_qna_003
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How do consumers perceive products with sustainability labels according to Hertz et al. (2017)?
nodes.answer: According to Hertz et al. (2017), the presence of a label does not automatically enhance the perception of a product.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Eco-label awareness_qna_004
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why is it important for consumers to understand sustainability labels according to Engels et al. (2010)?
nodes.answer: Engels et al. (2010) emphasize that consumers must understand the label for cross-product comparisons to make accurate sustainability choices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Eco-label awareness_qna_005
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How did Dior et al. (2021) measure consumers' knowledge gain through a cross-category environmental label?
nodes.answer: Dior et al. (2021) measured consumers' knowledge gain through a cross-category environmental label by evaluating the impact of the label on consumer awareness and understanding of environmental issues.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Eco-label awareness_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do consumer attitudes towards ecolabeled food products vary according to Gramsci et al. (2021)?
nodes.answer: According to Gramsci et al. (2021), consumer attitudes towards ecolabeled food products vary based on their purchasing motivations, as identified through latent class analysis.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Eco-label awareness_qna_007
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is a key factor in making the EU eco label effective, according to the text?
nodes.answer: The EU eco label will only be effective if citizens are well-equipped to understand and act upon the information communicated, highlighting the importance of citizen awareness and engagement.
